eligibilityPolicy.note: label eligibility for terminated KR securities, identity-blind by signature

value.appliesTo: label_eligibility is defined for ANY KR security; the SEALED completeness evidence it reads today only exists for the 22 KR securities named in alphaOpportunityV3SurvivorshipAudit's krTerminations list (a fact about which securities this repository has audited, not a fact the function branches on) -- for any other KR security `completeness=None` and a non-crossing window is ELIGIBLE, deferring to whatever total-return construction pipeline.korea_prices already applies to every KR security, exactly as v1-v3 already assumed for the whole KR universe. This is not a double standard: the 22 are excluded from PRODUCTION's implicit ELIGIBLE-by-default only because this repository has POSITIVELY MEASURED a gap for them (ZERO Yahoo dividend rows across their entire observed lives, against 215/238 dividend events on continuing names -- alphaOpportunityV3SurvivorshipAudit), not because they are the ones that terminate.

computedResultAsOfThisSeal.note: Computed by scripts/audit_alpha_opportunity_v4_kr_eligibility.py against the real sealed evidence -- not asserted. The NUMERIC result is unchanged from contract V1 (all 22 still excluded on both window scopes today) because the underlying per-security dividend/terminal-action evidence is exactly as incomplete as it was; what changed is that the MECHANISM computing this result no longer reads termination-list membership at all. Re-running this script against a repaired foundation would change this result without any change to the policy code or this spec.

value.correctionAppliedInThisRevision: The FIRST version of this policy (contract V1) branched on whether a security's code was in a `known_terminated_codes` set and, if so, excluded EVERY observation on it (pre- and post-termination) once its exDateSemanticsResolved read BLOCKED. That used the security's eventual termination status -- an outcome only knowable in hindsight -- as the gate deciding whether extra scrutiny applied to an observation whose own target window never touches the termination event, which is a future-survival-conditioned selection rule (a bounded, disclosed, but real instance of the same KIND of defect the US leg's NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE already named, even though the US case is structurally worse -- 0% coverage vs. a proven per-security data gap here). CONTRACT V2 removes `known_terminated_codes` and the security's own code from the eligibility FUNCTION entirely: `label_eligibility` takes only `completeness` (the sealed evidence row, or None if never audited) and `window_crosses_termination` (a pure calendar fact about the OBSERVATION's own target window, legitimate because a forward-return target is a claim about a bounded future interval by construction, exactly like the pre-existing MISSING_FORWARD_PRICE_OR_DELISTING check). Two securities with identical completeness evidence and the same window-crossing fact now receive IDENTICAL treatment regardless of whether one of them is known to terminate -- proved by tests/test_alpha_opportunity_v4.py's future-termination-invariance and future-metadata-mutation-invariance tests, which vary a synthetic terminates-later label while holding completeness fixed and assert the eligibility call does not move.
value.knownConsequence: v4's labeled sample excludes all 22 audited KR securities' observations entirely, at every signal date, under current evidence -- for a reason (a proven, per-security, zero-Yahoo-dividend-evidence data gap) that does not read termination status. This is NOT the same defect alpha-opportunity-model-v3 found in the US leg (NO_TERMINATED_SECURITY_IN_SAMPLE, where the panel never priced a departed name at all -- 0% coverage, structurally invisible): here the 22 names ARE priced, ARE members of the PIT KR universe on their live dates, and DO still enter feature computation and cross-sectional context -- only their own forward-return LABEL is withheld, for a disclosed, quantified, bounded and shrinking fraction of member-dates (alphaOpportunityV3SurvivorshipAudit: 3.7366% of tradable KR member-dates, 7.93% in 2013 declining to 0.76% in 2025). It is still a real, disclosed survivorship-adjacent limitation: v4's labeled sample never observes the realised forward outcome of a name whose OWN dividend evidence this repository has already found incomplete, which happens (for research-coverage reasons, not by rule) to be exactly the names that also terminate. `requiredDiagnostics.exclusionsClusterAroundTerminalEventsCheck` in evaluationPreregistration requires the future execution to publish this quantitatively rather than let it pass unremarked, and evaluationPreregistration's own verdict vocabulary must be read alongside this caveat, never as an unconditional statement about KR delisting risk.
neverAllowed: using a security's own eventual termination status, or list membership derived from it, as an input to any eligibility decision about a window that does not itself cross the termination event
treating an unresolved exchange ratio or successor as final
carrying the last traded price forward through a termination
inventing an ex-date from a record date or any other computed rule
assuming zero recovery for an unresolved termination
excluding or including an observation based on its realised return magnitude
using today's KR universe membership as a historical one
a new exclusion rule invented after an outcome is seen
value.rule: Non-crossing window (the target's own exit session is at or before the security's last traded session, or the security never terminates): ELIGIBLE if never audited (defers to production); if audited, ELIGIBLE only when exDateSemanticsResolved reads READY AND a total-return series has actually been spliced into the price panel used for labels (an engineering step this PR does not perform, so this is INELIGIBLE for every audited security today) -- never because the security is known to terminate. Crossing window (the target's own exit session is after the security's last traded session): requires terminationTypeResolved, terminalConsiderationResolved, successorResolvedWhereRequired (where the resolved type requires a successor) and terminalActionChainResolved all READY, and -- where a successor is required -- that successor's own price panel. This branch legitimately depends on the termination event because that event is INSIDE the target window being constructed.

universeWideCorroboration.interpretation: 224 of 226 (99.1%) DART-confirmed dividend-year rows across 25 outcome-blind-selected continuing names show at least one Yahoo dividend event in the same window; ZERO of the 25 show the specific all-years-zero pattern all 22 audited terminated names show. 010140.KS has no DART fiscal-year rows to check at all in this sample -- a data-absence case, category C (unknown from this evidence), neither counted as corroborating nor contradicting, and never assumed to be a genuine zero-dividend company or a vendor gap.
universeWideCorroboration.purpose: Not a full universe audit. Corroborates that treating `completeness is None` (the 213 continuing KR names never audited for dividend-basis completeness) as ELIGIBLE-by-deferral is an evidence-supported default, not a blind trust, and that the near-total Yahoo dividend blackout specific to the 22 audited terminated names is a real, distinctive, measured pattern rather than an artifact of asymmetric scrutiny alone.
universeWideCorroboration.scopeLimit: 213 of 238 continuing KR names, and all 118 REMOVED_FROM_INDEX_STILL_TRADING departed names, remain unaudited by ANY dividend-completeness check under either standard (DART ex-date confirmation or this lighter amount cross-validation). This is a disclosed, bounded research-coverage gap, never claimed to be closed by this corroboration sample, and a full-universe audit is separate, additive future data-foundation work, out of scope for this preregistration.
universeWideCorroboration.selectionMechanism: pipeline.kr_continuing_dividend_sample.select_continuing_sample: every code ranked inside the top-120 by market cap on at least one monthly snapshot, EXCLUDING the 22 terminated securities under study, ranked by how many snapshot dates it held that rank (most persistent first). Nothing about dividend completeness enters this ranking rule -- it was built to validate the DART-derivation methodology generally, before this correction ever needed it as corroborating evidence.

orderingStatistic.chronology: Made before any historical label, score or outcome was read for this study; it is recorded in this frozen file, not adopted after seeing a result.
orderingStatistic.decision: rankWeightedSpread is the CONFIRMATORY ordering statistic. Spearman rankIC is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY and can neither pass nor fail a claim.
orderingStatistic.definition: Per signal date, dollar-neutral weights w_i = centred within-date rank of the B4 predicted gross relative return divided by the sum of the positive centred ranks; rankWeightedSpread(t) = sum_i w_i * Y(t,i) with Y the gross forward relative return. Ties are broken by ticker ascending (stable order). Dates with fewer than minimumNamesPerDate names are excluded from the evaluation calendar, as inherited.
orderingStatistic.revisionOf: The earlier design expectation (alpha-research-design-review-v1 section 11 and alpha-opportunity-model-v2/v4 evaluation gate B) required a positive lower bound for mean within-date rank correlation.
orderingStatistic.why: rankIC ranks the forward target, is not linear in returns and cannot be attributed to calendar weeks, so no completed calibration covers it. rankWeightedSpread is linear in forward returns with weights fixed at the signal date and was calibrated (ALPHA_INFERENCE_CALIBRATION_V5, 24 of 24 cells). ALPHA_INFERENCE_CALIBRATION_V5 states that adopting it 'is a v5 design decision this protocol does not make'; this preregistration makes it.
